entries.notes: Italian surname: 'ci' before a vowel is the 'ch' sound, so chal-DEE-nee. Documented by pronunciation dictionaries (Forvo, Italian entry) and consistent with the author's own anglicised usage. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'sigh-al-DEE-ni' (sˌaɪəldˈiːnɪ), which is wrong.
Dutch given name pronounced yohst, documented by Forvo's Dutch entries. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'juiced' (dʒˈuːst). Case-sensitive to avoid touching unrelated words.
KAHN-yay, per the artist's own usage and pronunciation dictionaries. The unassisted phonemizer produced KAN-eye (kˈanaɪ).
The artist's name is universally jay-ZEE, including in British usage. The unassisted en-gb phonemizer produced jay-ZED (dʒˈeɪzˈɛd).
Italian surname, approximately SFORT-sa. The unassisted British phonemizer treated the initial letters as the word 'S' plus 'forza' and produced ess-FOR-za, so a dictionary override is required.
The given name uses the vowel in Calvin or cat. The unassisted British phonemizer produced an open back vowel closer to 'Karl'. Case-sensitive matching avoids unrelated lowercase text.
ROH-ling, like rolling without a strongly sounded second l. The unassisted British phonemizer produced ROU-ling with the vowel in 'out'.
gwi-DAR-ah, as the author says it in his own talks and podcast introductions. The unassisted phonemizer produced guy-DAR-ah (ɡaɪdˈɑːɹə).
MISH-uh-lin per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted phonemizer produced MITCH-i-lin (mˈɪtʃɪlˌɪn).
ih-LENG-kus, with the Greek chi as a hard k, per Merriam-Webster. The unassisted phonemizer produced ih-LEN-chus with a church-ch (ɪlˈɛntʃəs).
PLAY-toe per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted British phonemizer produced PLAH-toe (plˈɑːtəʊ). Case-sensitive to avoid touching unrelated lowercase text.
